description: Makes the running editor scan the project filesystem, so files written outside it are picked up. A scan or an import the editor is already running is waited out first rather than scanned over, which would start a second import over it. The scan is a change-detecting walk rather than an unconditional reparse, so a file another engine has already imported reads as settled and the walk does not look inside it: its class_name then stays out of the list the editor resolves against, however many times you scan. Any class in that state is named under unseenByEditor, which is what no check on disk can see, since the declaration and the cache are both correct there and only the editor disagrees. The cure is this call on its own, with no change to the declaring script, measured against a real editor on three platforms. editor_launch restart also does it and costs a window, and project_import refresh_classes does not: it rewrites the cache and does not touch what the editor is holding. The walk also passes over a file whose .uid alone changed, so the editor keeps the old UID and every engine reading its cache warns of a duplicate; before scanning, each file whose .uid names a UID the editor does not hold for it is read again and named under uidsReread, and files on disk naming one UID between them are named under uidsDuplicatedOnDisk, which reading again cannot settle. A class the scan brings in is named under broughtIn, and every script naming it is reloaded in the editor and named under dependentsReloaded: what the editor compiled from them while it could not see the class stays compiled that way after the scan, and a script extending a new base class went on reporting "Could not find base class" until reloaded. One that would not reload is named under dependentsNotReloaded and the call is not ok, as it is not when the script named in reloadScript was not reloaded. A script that fails to compile is tried again once the scripts it is compiled against that the editor holds behind their files are reloaded, which are named under reloadedFirst. An editor importing answers nothing until the import is over, and a hidden one imports on the thread that answers, so a large addon install can leave the rescan itself unanswered: that is waited for as any busy editor is, within timeoutMs, and when the wait runs out first the answer is stillWorking. The classes the editor could not see before that scan are then noted in the project, and the next editor_rescan of the same editor, from any server, names them under broughtIn and reloads what names them, which it could not otherwise know to do, since by then the editor sees them. A scan writes .godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg from the list the editor is holding, so a class the editor cannot resolve goes out of that file with it. That is not a reason to refuse the scan, because on a class the editor has merely not walked yet the scan is the cure; what the answer does instead is name the loss under cacheLost and rebuild the cache from the files, naming what came back under cacheRestored, so no fresh engine, CI run or clone inherits the short file. An editor that lost classes is still holding the short list, so the note says to restart it before scanning again. The other direction is guarded the same way: a class the editor still holds for a script that was renamed or deleted comes back into the cache at a path that is not there, and the next engine to read it fails on "Could not parse global class" in whichever correct script shares the bare name, so the cache is rebuilt without it and the answer names it under cacheDropped; the editor goes on holding it until it is restarted, and every scan until then ends in that rebuild. A script or shader written outside the editor has no .uid sidecar until something imports it, and the scan writes one beside it, which a project that commits sidecars needs before the commit. Needs the editor connected. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

listMembers.description: With reloadScript: also answer the whole member lists, heldBeforeReload and reloadedMethods for the methods, heldConstantsBeforeReload and reloadedConstants for the constants, each with what the script inherits from the scripts it extends. Default false: a script holding hundreds of constants answers hundreds of lines twice to say what one reload added.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

reloadScript.description: A script to recompile in the editor after the scan, for the half a scan does not reach: a script the editor has loaded keeps the copy it built, that copy is refreshed when one of its dependencies changes rather than when it changes itself, and a scan leaves it alone. Measured here, a built copy comes back without a method added to it while script_diagnostics on the same script reads clean in the same window, so the copy the editor built and whatever the analyser resolves types against are not known to be one thing: reload for the copy, and read the diagnostics as a separate answer rather than as this one confirmed. This recompiles into the same object, so the holders that kept the stale copy alive see the new one. What the reload changed comes back under methodsAdded, methodsRemoved, constantsAdded and constantsRemoved, with each enum value as Kind.SHORT among the constants, since an enum member is held as a constant and never shows among the methods; methodsHeld and constantsHeld count what the copy holds afterwards, because a reload that compiled nothing and answered OK is the failure worth catching. listMembers adds the whole lists. A script that does not compile is not reloaded: reloadProblem gives Godot's error, says whether the copy the editor holds survived, and names the classes the file uses, whose held copies being behind is what failed one before. A @tool script is not reloaded either, since it runs inside the editor and reloading one from inside a call can take the editor down: reloadProblem says so, and editor_launch restart recompiles it. A path spelled in another case than the file is reloaded under the spelling on disk, which is the one the editor holds its copy under, and that spelling comes back under reloadedAs. A script open in a script tab with unsaved edits is reloaded from the file all the same, and unsavedInEditorNote says that saving the tab writes its text back over the file; open tabs with no unsaved edits reread what changed, as they do when the editor's window takes the focus.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the scan. Default 30000.

name: editor_rescan
title: Rescan the project
